title: KCS U3c (c) RUN (rows 1e9/1e10/1e11): the LOS paper's r = 2, q = 4 data rows (arXiv:1603.03720v4, Lemke Oliver & Soundararajan, PNAS 2016, Section 5 - fetched and IDENTITY-CHECKED, persisted at tmp/u3c_c_fig/paper.pdf) cross-checked against an INDEPENDENT exact pair-class sieve (numpy odd sieve, the same clearing set as the 0186/0187 ground truth). All three checked rows AGREE at the paper's published precision: 1e9 pi(1,1) = 11,413,177 vs 1.141e7 (diff 3.2e3, tol 5e3), pi(1,3) = 14,010,314 vs 1.401e7 (diff 314); 1e10 pi(1,1) = 103,160,935 vs 1.032e8 (diff 3.9e4), pi(1,3) = 124,362,340 vs 1.244e8 (diff 3.8e4); 1e11 pi(1,1) = 941,199,658 vs 9.412e8 (diff 342), pi(1,3) = 1,117,820,622 vs 1.118e9 (diff 1.8e5, 3-fig-row tolerance 5e5), and pi(1e11) = 4,118,054,813 = the tabulated value (identity). NEW MEASURED STRUCTURE: pi(x;4,(1,3)) = pi(x;4,(3,1)) holds EXACTLY (diff = 0) at all three scales 1e9/1e10/1e11 - the paper's Conjecture 1.5 symmetry pi(a,b) = pi(-b,-a) + O(x^{1/2+epsilon}) is exact at these scales (the oscillating zero-sum is 0, or < 1, up to 1e11). Convention reconciliation: the recorded 'meas' census (gap-based, incl. the (2,3) gap) reproduces 0.551072/0.546585/0.542888 at 1e9/1e10/1e11 - the full U3b/U3c measurement pipeline re-derived from raw pair counts to ~5e-7 (display precision). Verdict: the paper's published data (their primesieve C++ pipeline) is independently CORROBORATED on 3 of its 4 rows; the 1e12 row (8.654e9 / 1.015e10) is the paper's highest and is IN PROGRESS (margin-verified 20-window 5e10 interval sieve, checkpointed, ~40 min, 1 core) - it will land as the next entry TOGETHER with the new 1e12 residual-ladder point, which is exactly the out-of-sample discriminator named in 0187/0190 between the 0186 4-point mixed form and the 0190 derived 2-term form. No RH claim: published-DATA cross-check + exact integer sieve; flank provenance work.
claim: U3c item (c), long the last OPEN item of the U3c spec ('check the paper's r = 2, q = 4 figure [data] against our rows; the text extraction did not capture the figure data'): the paper arXiv:1603.03720v4 (Lemke Oliver & Soundararajan, 'Unexpected biases in the distribution of consecutive primes', PNAS 2016, DOI 10.1073/pnas.1605366113) was re-fetched (the long-form PDF; the arXiv HTML v4 carries no figures - the 'r = 2, q = 4 data figure' is the Section 5 comparison TABLE of Actual vs (2.16) vs (5.1) values at x = 1e9, 1e10, 1e11, 1e12; provenance: tmp/u3c_c_fig/paper.pdf + paper.txt, title line identity-checked). Section 5 Actual rows for q = 4 (verbatim): 1e9: 1.141e7 / 1.401e7; 1e10: 1.032e8 / 1.244e8; 1e11: 9.412e8 / 1.118e9; 1e12: 8.654e9 / 1.015e10 (pi(x;4,(1,1)) / pi(x;4,(1,3))). Method: independent exact pair-class census under the PAPER convention (pi(x;q,(a,b)) = #{p_n <= x: p_n == a (mod q), p_{n+1} == b (mod q)}; p_n odd; successor unrestricted, seen by sieving x + margin; global numpy odd sieve with margin 400 at 1e9/1e10, margin-verified 2-window 5e10 interval sieve at 1e11 the 0187 machinery, boundary gap max 54 << margin 2000 verified). Results: 1e9: pi(1,1) = 11,413,177 (|diff| 3,180 <= tol 5,000 AGREE), pi(1,3) = 14,010,314 (|diff| 314 AGREE); 1e10: pi(1,1) = 103,160,935 (|diff| 39,065 <= 50,000 AGREE), pi(1,3) = 124,362,340 (|diff| 37,660 AGREE); 1e11: pi(1,1) = 941,199,658 (|diff| 342 AGREE), pi(1,3) = 1,117,820,622 (|diff| 179,378, within the 3-fig row tolerance 5e5 AGREE), pi(1e11) = 4,118,054,813 = tabulated value (identity). NEW: pi(1,3) - pi(3,1) = 0 EXACTLY at 1e9 (14,010,314 each), 1e10 (124,362,340 each) and 1e11 (1,117,820,622 each) - the Conjecture 1.5 antisymmetry holds exactly (the O(x^{1/2+eps}) zero-sum is empirically 0 at these scales); the diagonal is NOT symmetric: pi(3,3) - pi(1,1) = +551 (1e9) / +5,960 (1e10) / +14,252 (1e11) (growing slowly with x, measured). Convention reconciliation: 'meas' (the record's gap-class census over chains of consecutive primes both <= x, incl. the (2,3) gap counted in the denominator as 'even') = 0.551072 / 0.546585 / 0.542888 at 1e9/1e10/1e11 vs recorded 0.551072/0.546585/0.542888 (diff <= 5e-7, display) - the U3b/U3c measurement pipeline is re-derived from raw exact pair counts. In-flight (next entry): the 1e12 window run (20 x 5e10, checkpointed; started 2026-10-27 ~01:10, ~40 min ETA) checks the paper's 1e12 row AND produces the new 1e12 residual-ladder point R(1e12) = meas(1e12) - u3(1e12) - the named out-of-sample discriminator (0187/0190) between the 0186 4-pt mixed form (predicts +0.001851 at 1e12) and the 0190 derived 2-term form (predicts +0.003179 at 1e12): the predictions differ by +0.001328 ~ 500 se(1e12) - the 1e12 point separates them decisively. No RH claim: the paper's Main Conjecture remains a conjecture; this unit corroborates published DATA rows and measures exact integer counts; flank provenance work, no gating of the mainstream.
